record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: How can a peer-to-peer data-sharing system guarantee long-term file availability so that every stored file remains accessible regardless of which particular nodes are currently online and regardless of the file's popularity?

evidence.quote: We might like to ensure that all files stored in the system are always available regardless of which nodes in the network are currently online.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed peer-to-peer data-sharing system modeled as a dynamic network of nodes (peers), where at any given time only an unpredictable subset of nodes is online. Each file f in the system is stored at some collection of nodes, and a user requesting f succeeds if and only if at least one node currently online holds a retrievable copy (or sufficient encoded fragments) of f. Files vary widely in popularity, measured by request frequency, and may be requested arbitrarily rarely.

Design a protocol (specifying replication/erasure-coding, placement, maintenance/repair, and admission rules) and prove guarantees of the following form: for every file f ever inserted into the system and for every time t after its insertion, the probability (or worst-case guarantee under a specified churn model) that f is retrievable at time t is at least 1 − ε, where ε is a prescribed small constant, and where the guarantee holds:

(i) regardless of which particular subset of nodes is online at time t (subject to a stated bound on simultaneous offline nodes or a stated churn model), and
(ii) regardless of the popularity (request rate) of f, in particular for files that are essentially never requested.

State and prove the minimal assumptions on node availability, storage budget per node, bandwidth for repair, and network connectivity under which such perpetual availability is achievable, and prove matching impossibility results showing that without these assumptions no protocol can achieve perpetual availability for all files.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad systems-design problem about perpetual file availability in peer-to-peer storage. While many partial techniques exist (erasure coding, proactive repair as in TotalRecall, OceanStore, DHash, and academic analyses of churn), no single protocol with a fully proved guarantee of perpetual availability for arbitrary files under realistic churn has been established as a definitive solution. The status of the general question as posed is not conclusively settled; it remains an active research area rather than a closed theorem.

status_evidence.snippet: We might like to ensure that all files stored in the system are always available regardless of which nodes in the network are currently online.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of guaranteeing perpetual file availability is posed as an open problem.
